_doc: PILOT-MODEL-1 (owner question, 2026-11-12): who runs Ultrastable for a pilot customer, and what is the revenue model. Decision and hypotheses as data; consumed by scripts/build_dashboard.py (the pilot options panel on /dashboard) and checked by tests/foundation/test_dashboard.py. Prices are hypotheses to test with pilots, not advice or commitments.
why: The pilot runs in the customer's own Cloudflare (or other cloud) account, so the customer's data and secrets never touch our infrastructure. That removes our data-protection, encryption and multi-tenant isolation burden during the pilot and answers the buyer's first question (where does my data live) with 'in your account'. Ultrastable's own infrastructure only ever holds Ultrastable's own data, which is what the public dashboard shows.
revert: Offer the hosted option only after a pilot asks for it and the isolation, encryption and data-processing terms in the hosted option are built and reviewed; the model below keeps that as a separate, later tier.

options.setup: we help install; the loops then run there
options.revenue: paid pilot (fixed fee for setup and the first improvement cycles), then a monthly subscription for updates, managers' playbooks and support

options.our_data_burden: high: isolation, encryption, retention, processor terms
options.status: deferred until a pilot asks and the burden is built
options.name: multi-tenant hosted

options.revenue: core is source-available under the hybrid licence; charge for the managers' policy packs, the dashboard and support

pilot_proof_points: a second independent installation reports a tick (Q-GAP-second-installation)
the customer's own objectives and metrics are seeded and probed from day one (OBJECTIVES-1)
the first improvement the managers originated, measured before and after

hypotheses.claim: Buyers will pay a fixed pilot fee when the system runs in their own account and the first measured improvement is guaranteed in the agreement
Subscription is sustained by the improvement backlog the managers keep generating, not by hosting

program.title: Pilot applications
program.pitch: Applications are open for a small number of pilots with strong use cases and interesting demos of autonomous code loops and virtual agent managers. A pilot is a maintained system you already run or want to run, where the next improvement is not obvious and maintenance has become the burden.
selection: passes the system test in docs/doctrine/VISION.md: a loop to close, a measure that can be wrong, upkeep that never ends, a running cost you accept
has an owner who can state the objective and the few steps a person always decides
runs (or will run) in your own account, so your data stays with you
a use case that makes an interesting public demo, with your permission
program.you_get: Ultrastable installed on one system of yours: objectives and probes set up with you, the managers originating and shipping measured improvements, a dashboard of your own system, and the audit trail.
program.we_get: monthly feedback and permission to cite measured results
apply_fields: how you would know it is working
program.price: set per pilot while the market is tested (hypotheses H1 and H2); no list price is published yet

layers.title: Turtles all the way down
layers.rule: The same bootstrap, system test, objectives and probes apply at every level. A level reports up to its parent and runs its own loops; nothing at one level is special-cased.

levels.name: Ultrastable on itself
levels.what: the platform that runs its own roadmap, managers and probes (customer zero)

levels.name: A customer's system built on it
levels.what: a maintained system bootstrapped from an IDEA.md with parent: ultrastable

levels.name: Systems built on that system
levels.what: a platform a customer offers its own users, bootstrapped with parent: <their slug>

layers.roll_up: a child's liveness metrics are readable by its parent through an http probe; a child that stops reporting breaches M-parent-link at the parent

multi_tenant_obligations.status: deferred; a separate obligation, not a pilot feature
before_offering: tenant isolation proven by test (no query or binding crosses tenants)
encryption of tenant data at rest and in transit, key handling documented
data-processing agreement, subprocessor list, retention and deletion on request
per-tenant budget and kill switch so one tenant cannot spend another's allowance
